title: Stochastic resonance in time-delayed bistable active particles
authors: Antonio A. Valido, Mattia Coccolo, Miguel A. F. Sanjuán
abstract: We investigate analytically and numerically stochastic resonance in an underdamped active (Ornstein--Uhlenbeck) particle confined in a bistable potential with time-delayed feedback and subjected to an additional (non-thermal) white-noise source. Restricting the analysis to the active-noise-dominated bistable regime, with sufficiently short delay and active-noise correlation times, we develop a perturbative theory that yields analytical expressions for both the escape rate and the spectral power amplification within the framework of linear-response theory, without invoking detailed balance. The analytical predictions are in qualitative agreement with direct numerical simulations throughout the perturbative regime. We show that a moderate increase in the active-noise correlation time can enhance the stochastic-resonance response, in marked contrast to previous results for overdamped passive systems driven by colored noise. Conversely, the addition of white noise weakens the resonant response and shifts its optimum toward lower active-noise intensities. Time-delayed feedback further alters the matching condition between the escape rate and the driving frequency while preserving the resonant mechanism. Beyond the perturbative regime, we find that finite-memory effects progressively broaden the resonance profile and substantially decrease its amplitude. Overall, these results provide new insight into the combined role of inertia, activity, environmental fluctuations, and time delayed feedback in stochastic resonance in nonequilibrium systems.
summary: This work analyzes stochastic resonance in an active particle system subjected to time-delayed feedback and multiple noise sources. Using linear-response theory, the authors derive analytical predictions for the resonance behavior, revealing that active noise correlation time can enhance the effect, contrary to simpler models. The findings highlight the complex interplay between inertia, activity, and time delays in non-equilibrium physics.
main_problem: The paper investigates stochastic resonance (SR) in a complex, non-equilibrium system involving inertia, active fluctuations, time-delayed feedback, and environmental noise.
main_result: The study shows that active noise correlation time can enhance the SR response, while white noise weakens it; the analysis provides new insight into the combined role of inertia, activity, and time delay in non-equilibrium SR.
method: The authors developed a perturbative theory using the WKB approximation combined with linear-response theory to derive analytical expressions for the escape rate and spectral power amplification.
model_or_system: The system is an underdamped active particle (Ornstein--Uhlenbeck process) confined in a bistable potential that includes a time-delayed feedback term. The dynamics are driven by both non-thermal active noise and environmental white noise.
key_observables: Escape rate and Spectral Power Amplification (SPA).

main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to the active-noise-dominated regime and relies on perturbative approximations valid for short delays and weak noise intensities.

paper_structure: The paper builds from defining the complex stochastic differential equations governing the particle's motion to developing the perturbative theory, deriving analytical expressions for observables like SPA, and finally comparing these theoretical predictions with numerical simulations.
why_interesting: The inclusion of active noise and time-delayed feedback moves the study beyond standard passive, thermal systems, offering insights into non-equilibrium dynamics relevant to active matter and open quantum systems.
